title: 過去形の本質は距離感
prompt:
Create a polished content-rich educational English grammar page in portrait 9:16, matching the supplied cover's energetic explorer design. Same leopard mascot measuring distance from NOW and using a soft request cushion. No page number, source name, watermark, or logo.

Top Japanese title: 「過去形の本質は距離感」

Central mechanism: past tense places an event on a separated past island; the same distance can soften a present wish/request by reducing direct pressure. Distinguish literal past from polite distancing through context.

Original examples:
• The alarm rang at midnight. 「今から切り離された過去」
• We lived near the harbor in 2019. 「完結した過去の期間」
• I wanted to ask if you had a moment. 「今の依頼を控えめに」
• Did you need any help? 「今の相手へ柔らかく確認」

Show pressure gauge: “I want to ask...” direct → “I wanted to ask...” more tentative. Note that polite past does not necessarily mean the desire ended.

Mini practice: does “I hoped you could help me” always describe an old hope? Answer: no; reason 「現在の依頼から心理的距離を取ることがある」.

Takeaway: 「過去形は、時間にも気持ちにも一歩の距離を作る」.
